bull_bear.body: Board approved 5:1 bonus share issue (record date June 24, 2026) to enhance liquidity; Final dividend INR 4/share post-bonus recommended; reinvestment in R&D and manufacturing maturity assessments.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Geopolitical conflict in West Asia disrupting supply chains; US tariffs impacting export competitiveness; Aluminum/copper price volatility; Delay in 2027 regulation implementation; Diesel price hikes potentially dampening CV demand.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident on long-term structural growth driven by safety regulations and localization; cautious on near-term margins due to macro volatility; disciplined execution highlighted despite supply chain constraints.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Q3 FY26 value-per-vehicle (INR 45.5k) was artificially inflated by one-time retrospective price recoveries, normalizing to INR 39.5k in Q4; voluntary ESC fitment currently limited to hazardous goods (POL) tankers ahead of 2027 mandate; rainwater harvesting at Jamshedpur meets 40% of plant water needs, reducing operational risk.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Complete system solution provider that uniquely connects truck, trailer, cargo, drivers, business partners and fleet operators in real-time to enhance fleet safety and operational efficiency
- Dedicated ESC test track in Chennai enabling end-to-end ESC solutions - application engineering, pre-homologation support and validation - accelerating regulatory readiness
- Engineering base of over 1,000 engineers contributing to both global programmes and India-specific needs
- Access to global technology and R&D through ultimate holding company ZF Friedrichshafen AG
- Pan-India Authorized Service Centre (ASC) network of around 280 service centers supporting aftermarket reach
- Broadest range of commercial vehicle solutions across Automated Driving, Electric Mobility, Safety and Connected/Shared Transportation and Fleet Operations' Digitalization
- Export presence in 18 countries across the Americas, Asia, Europe and Africa (36.61% of turnover)
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Cyclicality of the Indian commercial vehicle industry — Management explicitly flags that the cyclical nature of the Indian commercial vehicle industry presents its own risk to the business, given the Company's revenue is closely tied to CV demand cycles.
- Raw material / commodity price volatility (steel, iron ore, aluminium) — Domestic HRC steel prices rose from Rs 46,000/MT to Rs 53,800/MT and remain volatile; aluminium prices are expected to stay elevated through 2026 on structural supply deficits and EV/infrastructure demand; iron ore import costs are rising due to a domestic shortage of high-quality raw material - all of which pressure input costs for an auto-component manufacturer.
- Geopolitical and global trade policy uncertainty — The Middle East conflict is driving up Indian iron ore prices and freight/fuel-related delivery costs, and geopolitical tensions and supply chain disruptions are flagged as headwinds that could impact raw material and energy prices, with implications for vehicle prices and fleet profitability.
- Customer collections / working-capital risk — The Company notes it is receiving major dues from customers 'albeit with some minor delays' and has resorted to bank payment arrangements on a selective basis for some customers, indicating some receivables/collection risk despite an otherwise strong liquidity position.
- Whistle-blower / conduct complaints — Ten whistle blower complaints were received during FY 2025-26 under the Company's Vigil Mechanism / Whistle Blower Policy, a governance watch-item even though the Company describes robust ERM and Code of Conduct processes.
- Concentration / dependency on ZF Group related-party transactions — The Company's business is materially intertwined with its ultimate holding company's group - notably recurring material related-party transactions with fellow subsidiary ZF CV Systems Global GmbH requiring shareholder postal-ballot approval each year - creating a structural dependency on intra-group pricing and transaction terms (goods, services and license fee arrangements marked up on cost).
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: OE Sales: +17.6% FY26 (INR 1,978cr); Aftermarket: +15.6% FY26 (INR 584cr), driven by network expansion; Exports (Goods): -11.1% FY26 (INR 1,025cr) due to US tariff headwinds; Export Services: +15.4% FY26 (INR 509cr).

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body: The Company manufactures automotive components - air assist and full air actuation systems and accessories - for commercial vehicles and trailer fleets, partnering with OEMs, fleets and the aftermarket to deliver braking, safety, electric-mobility and fleet-digitalisation technologies across the vehicle's lifecycle. FY26 turnover mix: manufacturing of automotive components ~72.59%, spares ~14.25%, software services/R&D/business services ~11.40%.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **OEM / Automotive Components:** Exhaust Brake Valve, E-Compressor / electric compressor, ABS/EBS braking system, OPR (Optimised Power Reduction) compressor, Clutch servo with sensor, Electronic Stability Control (ESC), Automated Manual Transmission (AMT), Tire Pressure Monitoring System (TPMS), Trailer EBS, Advanced Air Processing Units, Electronically Controlled Air Suspension (ECAS)
- **Aftermarket:** Air suspension with ECAS technology, Tandem master cylinder, Clutch master cylinders, Diesel Exhaust Fluid (DEF)
- **Spares:** Automotive component spares

latest_quarter.body: Q4 margin pressure from 18% spike in aluminum prices (INR 233 to INR 274/kg) and Jan 1 salary hikes; recovery negotiations with OEMs ongoing but lagging; cost inflation disproportionately impacted EBITDA growth vs revenue.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue Growth: Cautious momentum for FY27 supported by GST tailwinds; Margin: Expected flattish to low single-digit growth due to commodity volatility; Order Inflow: Strong pipeline for ESC/ADAS ahead of 2027 mandates; Capex: INR 180-190cr planned for new products and upgrades.
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Secured full-suite ADAS/ESC business awards from 2 major OEMs for upcoming 2027 regulations; ongoing technical benchmarking with multiple other OEMs; retrofit demand for trailer EBS in oil & gas segment.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Mandatory ESC/AEBS regulation for >6T vehicles from Oct 2027; EV compressor/EBS penetration in electric buses; Localization of global ZF sourcing to India amid high EU energy costs; Trailer safety tech adoption (AIS-113).
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Position as a complete system solution provider that connects truck, trailer, cargo, drivers, business partners and fleet operators in real-time to enhance fleet safety and operational efficiency
- Work with OEMs to reduce Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) via value enhancers and improved fleet uptime through Fleet Management Solutions
- Increase per-vehicle content and technology penetration, and foray into new domains of commercial vehicle technology, to sustain and grow revenues
- Refined strategic focus on the LCV (e-LCV) segment to establish and solidify market leadership
- Partner with trailer customers to implement 100% TABS penetration and expand the Intelligent Trailer Program and air disc brakes for trailers
- Close association with OEMs on implementing ADAS as a regulatory requirement, to retain market position
- Provide technical / homologation support for advanced technology products
- Leverage or expand manufacturing footprint to ensure increased customer centricity
- Increase penetration of new products - Automated Manual Transmission, door control system, Trailer Lift Axle Suspension Systems, Air Disc Brakes
- Introduce new business and revenue models through e-commerce in the aftermarket business, and ramp up sales, service and distribution network
- Expand the pan-India Authorized Service Centre (ASC) network (currently around 280 service centers)
- Strategic capex investments to expand crankshaft manufacturing capabilities to meet rising domestic demand and support exports
- Strengthen export portfolio through expansion of air processing units and cartridge offerings to access new markets and revenue streams
- Continued evaluation of make-versus-buy decisions across the supply chain and capital investment programs to enhance cost competitiveness
- Fund the e-compressor business through preference share investments in the wholly owned subsidiary for efficient capital deployment
- Bonus issue aimed at broadening retail investor participation and improving trading liquidity
- Focus on working capital excellence through inventory management, receivables control and supply chain financing solutions
- For FY 2025-26, the Board recommended a dividend of INR 4 per equity share, placed before shareholders for approval at the 22nd AGM (Notice of AGM), payable to shareholders on record as of the fixed record date.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: During FY 2025-26, the Company incurred capital expenditure of INR 123.64 crores against a planned estimate of INR 190 crores; the unspent INR 35.1 crores (relating to projects deferred from FY26) is expected to be utilised in FY 2026-27, alongside a fresh capex plan of INR 185.32 crores for FY 2026-27. To navigate a complex global environment of geopolitical disruptions, supply-chain constraints and rising commodity costs (aluminium, gas, chips and semiconductor components), the Company enhanced capacity across its value chain, scaled up hydraulic and pneumatic ESC systems, expanded e-compressor supplies for the domestic market, and strengthened its global footprint through higher-capacity compressor exports to Europe; new actuator variants for trailer platforms were also introduced. The future-ready product portfolio was enhanced with the launch of eight new products and an accelerated ramp-up across five key product lines, including new variants of the Exhaust Brake Valve, an Optimised Power Reduction (OPR) compressor, and advanced systems such as Electronic Braking System (EBS) and Electronically Controlled Air Suspension (ECAS) for electric buses. On the sustainability/infrastructure side, the Company commissioned a 1,200 KL rainwater harvesting pond at its Jamshedpur facility as part of its water-positive journey, alongside Zero Liquid Discharge (ZLD) systems across plants.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Commercial vehicle (CV) industry grew 11% in FY26 (medium-duty +23%, heavy-duty +7.9%), aided by strong GDP growth and consumption recovery following GST reforms and RBI rate cuts
- Aging vehicle fleet - nearly 42% of trucks are over 12 years old - creating a strong, multi-year replacement cycle
- E-commerce-led growth: ~25% of new CV sales estimated to be driven through online channels, with e-commerce market expected to grow at a CAGR of ~15% to reach USD 345 billion by 2030
- Digitalization and connectivity: growing adoption of telematics and fleet management systems opening new opportunities across the CV value chain
- Emerging business models: rise of freight aggregators and logistics platforms creating incremental CV demand
- Trailer industry formalization - transition from unorganized to organized players, with a surge in demand for specialized trailers including refrigerated units
- Shift in public transport procurement models: State Transport Undertakings migrating from CAPEX-based procurement to PPP and Gross Cost Contract models (around 18% as of 2023)
- Policy support: Vehicle Scrappage Policy, green mobility measures and the PM-eBus Sewa scheme accelerating replacement of older, polluting vehicles
- Regulatory tailwinds: mandatory ESC for buses, ADAS mandate for M2/M3 buses and N2/N3 trucks, growing TABS/EBS demand in hazardous goods carriers, and AC-cabin mandate for M2/M3 vehicles
- Government focus on sustainable mobility driving adoption of CNG/LNG and zero-emission technologies (BEV, FCEV, H2 ICE); PM E-drive scheme (Oct'24-Mar'26) expected to boost EV bus adoption, especially within State Transport Undertakings
- e-LCV segment experiencing rapid growth on robust B2B logistics demand, with projected 15% e-LCV market penetration by 2030
- Infrastructure expansion (express highways) generating demand for commercial vehicles with higher capacity engines and AMT systems in the heavy-duty segment; recent regulatory approval for vehicles up to 25.25m expected to drive Road Train adoption
- Rising input costs: Middle East conflict driving up Indian iron ore prices and freight/fuel-related delivery costs; aluminium prices expected to remain elevated through 2026 on structural supply deficits and EV/infrastructure demand; domestic shredded scrap prices expected to rise ~2.7% in early 2026
- Cyclical nature of the Indian commercial vehicle industry presents an inherent risk to the business
- Inventory turnover moderated to 10.20 times (from 12.45 times) due to supply constraints from geopolitical developments, reflecting higher inventory holding to support capacity readiness for increased demand
- Working capital increased 20.50% YoY, reflecting scale-up of business operations and support for growing revenue requirements
- Strong liquidity position and cash reserves mean the Company does not foresee a need to borrow or raise capital; strict cost control measures imposed to reduce discretionary spend amid cost pressures
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: ZF CV India delivered record FY26 revenue (+9.2%) and PAT (+12.2%) driven by domestic CV recovery and safety regulation uptake, though Q4 margins compressed 230bps QoQ due to aluminum inflation and wage hikes. The strategic pivot to mandatory ESC/AEBS by 2027 and a 5:1 bonus issue signal confidence, despite near-term export headwinds from US tariffs and geopolitical supply chain disruptions.

risks.risk: Cyclicality of the Indian commercial vehicle industry
risks.note: Management explicitly flags that the cyclical nature of the Indian commercial vehicle industry presents its own risk to the business, given the Company's revenue is closely tied to CV demand cycles.

risks.risk: Raw material / commodity price volatility (steel, iron ore, aluminium)
risks.note: Domestic HRC steel prices rose from Rs 46,000/MT to Rs 53,800/MT and remain volatile; aluminium prices are expected to stay elevated through 2026 on structural supply deficits and EV/infrastructure demand; iron ore import costs are rising due to a domestic shortage of high-quality raw material - all of which pressure input costs for an auto-component manufacturer.

risks.risk: Geopolitical and global trade policy uncertainty
risks.note: The Middle East conflict is driving up Indian iron ore prices and freight/fuel-related delivery costs, and geopolitical tensions and supply chain disruptions are flagged as headwinds that could impact raw material and energy prices, with implications for vehicle prices and fleet profitability.

The Company notes it is receiving major dues from customers 'albeit with some minor delays' and has resorted to bank payment arrangements on a selective basis for some customers, indicating some receivables/collection risk despite an otherwise strong liquidity position.

Ten whistle blower complaints were received during FY 2025-26 under the Company's Vigil Mechanism / Whistle Blower Policy, a governance watch-item even though the Company describes robust ERM and Code of Conduct processes.

risks.risk: Concentration / dependency on ZF Group related-party transactions
risks.note: The Company's business is materially intertwined with its ultimate holding company's group - notably recurring material related-party transactions with fellow subsidiary ZF CV Systems Global GmbH requiring shareholder postal-ballot approval each year - creating a structural dependency on intra-group pricing and transaction terms (goods, services and license fee arrangements marked up on cost).

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: ZF Commercial Vehicle Control Systems India Limited (ZF CVCS) is a technology leader shaping the future of commercial vehicle transportation systems, offering the broadest range of CV solutions across Automated Driving, Electric Mobility, Safety, and Connected/Shared Transportation & Fleet …

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: The Company manufactures automotive components - air assist and full air actuation systems and accessories - for commercial vehicles and trailer fleets, partnering with OEMs, fleets and the aftermarket to deliver braking, safety, electric-mobility and fleet-digitalisation technologies across the vehicle's lifecycle. FY26 turnover mix: manufacturing of automotive components ~72.59%, spares ~14.25%, software services/R&D/business services ~11.40%.

group_structure.title: Group structure (profile)
group_structure.body:
- ZF Friedrichshafen AG — related party: Ultimate holding company; Nil shares held by the listed entity
- WABCO Asia Private Limited, Singapore — related party: Holding company; holds 60% of the listed entity's shares
- ZF International UK Limited, United Kingdom — associate: Associate of the holding company
- ZF CV Control Systems Manufacturing India Private Limited — subsidiary: Wholly owned subsidiary of the Company (100% shareholding); also transacts with the Company as a related party
- Fellow subsidiaries of the ZF Friedrichshafen AG / WABCO group — related party: Numerous fellow subsidiary companies across the USA, Korea, China, Germany, Switzerland, Poland, Brazil, Thailand, Japan, Belgium, France, Dubai and India with which the Company had related-party transactions (purchase/sale of goods, services, licensing) during FY 2025-26, including WABCO Compressor Manufacturing Co. (USA), ZF CV Systems Global GmbH (Switzerland), ZF India Private Limited, ZF Digital Solutions India Private Limited, ZF Light Vehicle Systems India Private Limited, ZF Commercial Vehicle Solutions India Private Limited, ZF Rane Automotive India Private Limited, ZF Wind Power Coimbatore Private Limited, ZF CV Distribution Germany GmbH & Co. KG, ZF CV Systems Europe BV, ZF CV Systems North America LLC, ZF Automotive Systems (Shanghai) Co Ltd, WABCO Holdings Inc. and others

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:

order_book.title: Order book & pipeline
order_book.body: Secured full-suite ADAS/ESC business awards from 2 major OEMs for upcoming 2027 regulations; ongoing technical benchmarking with multiple other OEMs; retrofit demand for trailer EBS in oil & gas segment.

guidance.title: Guidance
guidance.body: Revenue Growth: Cautious momentum for FY27 supported by GST tailwinds; Margin: Expected flattish to low single-digit growth due to commodity volatility; Order Inflow: Strong pipeline for ESC/ADAS ahead of 2027 mandates; Capex: INR 180-190cr planned for new products and upgrades.

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: Mandatory ESC/AEBS regulation for >6T vehicles from Oct 2027; EV compressor/EBS penetration in electric buses; Localization of global ZF sourcing to India amid high EU energy costs; Trailer safety tech adoption (AIS-113).

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Commercial vehicle (CV) industry grew 11% in FY26 (medium-duty +23%, heavy-duty +7.9%), aided by strong GDP growth and consumption recovery following GST reforms and RBI rate cuts
- Aging vehicle fleet - nearly 42% of trucks are over 12 years old - creating a strong, multi-year replacement cycle
- E-commerce-led growth: ~25% of new CV sales estimated to be driven through online channels, with e-commerce market expected to grow at a CAGR of ~15% to reach USD 345 billion by 2030
- Digitalization and connectivity: growing adoption of telematics and fleet management systems opening new opportunities across the CV value chain
- Emerging business models: rise of freight aggregators and logistics platforms creating incremental CV demand
- Trailer industry formalization - transition from unorganized to organized players, with a surge in demand for specialized trailers including refrigerated units
- Shift in public transport procurement models: State Transport Undertakings migrating from CAPEX-based procurement to PPP and Gross Cost Contract models (around 18% as of 2023)
- Policy support: Vehicle Scrappage Policy, green mobility measures and the PM-eBus Sewa scheme accelerating replacement of older, polluting vehicles
- Regulatory tailwinds: mandatory ESC for buses, ADAS mandate for M2/M3 buses and N2/N3 trucks, growing TABS/EBS demand in hazardous goods carriers, and AC-cabin mandate for M2/M3 vehicles
- Government focus on sustainable mobility driving adoption of CNG/LNG and zero-emission technologies (BEV, FCEV, H2 ICE); PM E-drive scheme (Oct'24-Mar'26) expected to boost EV bus adoption, especially within State Transport Undertakings
- e-LCV segment experiencing rapid growth on robust B2B logistics demand, with projected 15% e-LCV market penetration by 2030
- Infrastructure expansion (express highways) generating demand for commercial vehicles with higher capacity engines and AMT systems in the heavy-duty segment; recent regulatory approval for vehicles up to 25.25m expected to drive Road Train adoption
- Rising input costs: Middle East conflict driving up Indian iron ore prices and freight/fuel-related delivery costs; aluminium prices expected to remain elevated through 2026 on structural supply deficits and EV/infrastructure demand; domestic shredded scrap prices expected to rise ~2.7% in early 2026
- Cyclical nature of the Indian commercial vehicle industry presents an inherent risk to the business
- Inventory turnover moderated to 10.20 times (from 12.45 times) due to supply constraints from geopolitical developments, reflecting higher inventory holding to support capacity readiness for increased demand
- Working capital increased 20.50% YoY, reflecting scale-up of business operations and support for growing revenue requirements
- Strong liquidity position and cash reserves mean the Company does not foresee a need to borrow or raise capital; strict cost control measures imposed to reduce discretionary spend amid cost pressures

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Q4 margin pressure from 18% spike in aluminum prices (INR 233 to INR 274/kg) and Jan 1 salary hikes; recovery negotiations with OEMs ongoing but lagging; cost inflation disproportionately impacted EBITDA growth vs revenue.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Board approved 5:1 bonus share issue (record date June 24, 2026) to enhance liquidity; Final dividend INR 4/share post-bonus recommended; reinvestment in R&D and manufacturing maturity assessments.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: During FY 2025-26, the Company incurred capital expenditure of INR 123.64 crores against a planned estimate of INR 190 crores; the unspent INR 35.1 crores (relating to projects deferred from FY26) is expected to be utilised in FY 2026-27, alongside a fresh capex plan of INR 185.32 crores for FY 2026-27. To navigate a complex global environment of geopolitical disruptions, supply-chain constraints and rising commodity costs (aluminium, gas, chips and semiconductor components), the Company enhanced capacity across its value chain, scaled up hydraulic and pneumatic ESC systems, expanded e-compressor supplies for the domestic market, and strengthened its global footprint through higher-capacity compressor exports to Europe; new actuator variants for trailer platforms were also introduced. The future-ready product portfolio was enhanced with the launch of eight new products and an accelerated ramp-up across five key product lines, including new variants of the Exhaust Brake Valve, an Optimised Power Reduction (OPR) compressor, and advanced systems such as Electronic Braking System (EBS) and Electronically Controlled Air Suspension (ECAS) for electric buses. On the sustainability/infrastructure side, the Company commissioned a 1,200 KL rainwater harvesting pond at its Jamshedpur facility as part of its water-positive journey, alongside Zero Liquid Discharge (ZLD) systems across plants.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident on long-term structural growth driven by safety regulations and localization; cautious on near-term margins due to macro volatility; disciplined execution highlighted despite supply chain constraints.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Complete system solution provider that uniquely connects truck, trailer, cargo, drivers, business partners and fleet operators in real-time to enhance fleet safety and operational efficiency
- Dedicated ESC test track in Chennai enabling end-to-end ESC solutions - application engineering, pre-homologation support and validation - accelerating regulatory readiness
- Engineering base of over 1,000 engineers contributing to both global programmes and India-specific needs
- Access to global technology and R&D through ultimate holding company ZF Friedrichshafen AG
- Pan-India Authorized Service Centre (ASC) network of around 280 service centers supporting aftermarket reach
- Broadest range of commercial vehicle solutions across Automated Driving, Electric Mobility, Safety and Connected/Shared Transportation and Fleet Operations' Digitalization
- Export presence in 18 countries across the Americas, Asia, Europe and Africa (36.61% of turnover)

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Geopolitical conflict in West Asia disrupting supply chains; US tariffs impacting export competitiveness; Aluminum/copper price volatility; Delay in 2027 regulation implementation; Diesel price hikes potentially dampening CV demand.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Q3 FY26 value-per-vehicle (INR 45.5k) was artificially inflated by one-time retrospective price recoveries, normalizing to INR 39.5k in Q4; voluntary ESC fitment currently limited to hazardous goods (POL) tankers ahead of 2027 mandate; rainwater harvesting at Jamshedpur meets 40% of plant water needs, reducing operational risk.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Position as a complete system solution provider that connects truck, trailer, cargo, drivers, business partners and fleet operators in real-time to enhance fleet safety and operational efficiency
- Work with OEMs to reduce Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) via value enhancers and improved fleet uptime through Fleet Management Solutions
- Increase per-vehicle content and technology penetration, and foray into new domains of commercial vehicle technology, to sustain and grow revenues
- Refined strategic focus on the LCV (e-LCV) segment to establish and solidify market leadership

themes.title: Auto components & EV-driveline localization
themes.need: Premiumization, content-per-vehicle rise and EV/hybrid transition pull a deep auto-ancillary chain - MOTHERSON/SONACOMS/BOSCHLTD/SCHAEFFLER/SKFINDIA/UNOMINDA-tier on driveline, bearings, wiring (MSUMI) and EV systems; OLAELEC/ATHERENERG/OLECTRA on EV OEMs (OLAELEC targeting cell-to-pack 10-15% cost edge); SUNDRMFAST/ENDURANCE/CRAFTSMAN/BHARATFORG on forgings/machining. Q1FY27 showed contracted pricing finally landing for Tier-2s: SSWL earned EBITDA/wheel of Rs 314 against Rs 262 YoY, which management attributed mostly to two years of OEM input-price increases finally landing (1-5%, more pending) rather than mix, with all plants above 95% utilisation and knuckles at 100%; KROSS delivered a 12.23% EBITDA margin (+63bps) BEFORE two retrospective pass-throughs land (steel settled ~15 July, the CV conversion-cost settlement still pending), making Q1 a floor rather than a peak.
themes.driver: GST 2.0 demand pull; retrospective OEM price pass-throughs still to land (KROSS CV conversion cost); EV cell/Gigafactory ramps (OLAELEC 6GWh by June); export + new-platform content wins.

themes.title: Auto OEM cycle - CV replacement & PV premiumization
themes.need: GST 2.0 rate rationalization plus an aged CV fleet still frames the replacement cycle, but Q1FY27's real signal is 2W OEMs EXPANDING margin through a commodity shock. TVSMOTOR sold 1.63mn units (+28%) on INR 13,896cr revenue (+38%) while lifting EBITDA margin 30bps to 12.8% having absorbed a ~4% commodity shock with only ~1.5% of price increase (CARE upgraded it AA+ to AAA), and committed 2W capacity from 6.8mn to 8.3mn by Q4FY27. BAJAJ-AUTO set volume/revenue/EBITDA records with margin at 20.9% (+110bps) through ~4.5% commodity inflation AND ~10% of volume lost to a ransomware shutdown, with EV now 30% of domestic revenue at double-digit EBITDA and Chetak EBITDA-positive - a scaled, profitable EV second engine. Commercial mobility is electrifying fastest: TVSMOTOR's 3W EV penetration crossed 40% for the first time. ASHOKLEY's all-time-high CV volumes (220k units, MHCV share 30.8%) carry the CV leg with defence + Switch EV optionality; TMCV/TMPV/SMLMAH/ESCORTS on CV/tractors; APOLLOTYRE/JKTYRE/BALKRISIND/MRF on tyres.
